answer_q: What is AI training for business?
answer: AI training for business teaches employees how to use AI tools productively and responsibly in their actual roles. Good training covers how the tools work, how to write effective prompts, how to check AI output, what information must never be shared, and which tasks AI should and shouldn’t do.
body:
Why generic AI courses don’t stick

Online AI courses explain what large language models are and show impressive demos. Then staff go back to their desks and don’t know how any of it applies to quoting a job, answering a client or preparing a month-end report. Adoption fades within weeks. Training sticks when it uses the participants’ real tasks, the tools they actually have access to and the rules your business has set.

That is how we run every session. Before training, we learn what each team does, which tools are approved and what your AI usage policy allows. Participants then practise on their own work during the session.

What staff learn

  1. How AI tools work in plain English, including why they sometimes produce confident errors.
  2. Prompting that works: giving context, examples and a clear format, and iterating instead of starting over.
  3. Checking output: verifying facts, figures and citations before anything leaves the business.
  4. Privacy and confidentiality: what must never be pasted into AI tools, following the OAIC’s guidance and your policy.
  5. Role-specific workflows: drafting, summarising, analysing data, writing proposals, preparing reports and answering customers.
  6. When not to use AI: decisions about people, sensitive client matters and anything requiring professional judgement.

Training formats

FormatLengthBest for
Leadership briefing90 minutesOwners and managers deciding how AI fits the business
Team workshopHalf dayHands-on practice for one team on its real tasks
Whole-of-business programSeveral sessions over four to six weeksRolling out AI tools across departments
AI champions programOngoingTraining internal champions to support their colleagues

Workshops run in person at your office anywhere in Greater Melbourne, or live online for teams elsewhere in Australia. Groups are kept small enough that everyone gets hands-on time.

Training by role

  • Sales and business development: account research, proposal drafts, follow-up emails and call preparation.
  • Operations and admin: procedures, checklists, rosters and summarising long email threads.
  • Finance: spreadsheet formulas, variance explanations and report commentary, with careful checking.
  • Marketing: content outlines, campaign ideas, social posts and repurposing content in your brand voice.
  • Customer service: reply drafts, tone adjustments and knowledge-base articles.
  • Managers: meeting summaries, planning documents and coaching staff on responsible use.

What participants take away

  • A prompt library for their role, tested during the session
  • A one-page cheat sheet on safe use and checking output
  • Access to custom assistants set up for their team, where relevant
  • A follow-up session to answer questions after real-world use

Responsible AI, built in

Every session reflects Australia’s AI Ethics Principles and the human-oversight practices in the Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption. Staff learn that AI drafts and people decide.

Measuring the impact of AI training

We survey participants before and after training on confidence and time spent on target tasks, and check tool adoption a few weeks later. Many teams identify tasks worth automating during training; those can move into AI automation projects so the savings scale beyond individual use.

How to book AI training

  1. Free AI audit to understand your teams, tools and goals.
  2. Training plan with formats, dates and a fixed price in AUD.
  3. Preparation: we gather sample tasks and tailor exercises.
  4. Delivery on site or online.
  5. Follow-up session and adoption check.

Common questions staff ask in training

The same questions come up in almost every session. Will AI replace my job? How do I know if the answer is right? Can I paste a client email in? Is it cheating to use AI for a report? We answer them directly. AI takes over drafting and repetitive tasks, but people stay accountable for decisions and anything that leaves the business. Answers need checking, especially facts, figures and quotes. Client and personal information only goes into tools the business has approved for that purpose. And using AI is fine when your policy allows it and you check the result, just as you would check a junior colleague’s draft.

Addressing these concerns openly is often what turns hesitant staff into confident users. It also gives managers a consistent way to talk about AI with their teams after the training ends.

We also leave managers with a short guide on reinforcing good AI habits in team meetings and one-on-ones.
faqs: Do staff need technical skills for AI training?
No. Our training is designed for everyday business users. If someone can write an email and use a web browser, they can learn to use AI tools well.
Can you train our team on Microsoft Copilot specifically?
Yes. We tailor training to the tools you have approved, including Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude and Google Gemini, using your own documents and tasks.
Do you run AI training in person in Melbourne?
Yes. We run workshops at client offices across Greater Melbourne, and live online sessions for teams elsewhere in Australia.
How much does AI training cost?
It depends on the format, number of sessions and group size. We provide a fixed quote in AUD after a free 30-minute audit.
